column1: # Numbers on the marketing site that read as a measurement, and where each
# one comes from.
# Three tab separated fields: the file, the figure exactly as figurecheck
# reports it, and why it is allowed to be there. A reason is required, because
# an exemption with no argument behind it is indistinguishable from somebody
# silencing a finding they did not understand. An exemption that stops being
# needed is reported, so this list cannot rot.
# The reason has to be true, and that is the whole mechanism. A figure from a
# shaped example says so, and the page says so too. A figure computed at build
# time says what computes it. A figure quoting somebody else names the source.
# A number nobody can source cannot be given a truthful reason here, and the
# answer is then to delete the number rather than to invent a reason for it.
# The fabricated fidelity score this gate was written for would have needed a
# row, and there was nothing true to write in it.
# Every row below is the same case: an example run drawn in a film or a panel,
# captioned on the page as chosen rather than measured. None of them is a
# claim about how well the product performs.
www/components/home/visuals/FirewallScene.tsx
column3: a CPU reading on the mock service dashboard the firewall film draws. Set dressing inside an illustration, not a measurement of anything.

column1: www/components/home/visuals/ReportScene.tsx
column3: the latency line of the shaped run this film types out. The page captions it as one shaped run whose numbers were chosen, not measured.

column1: www/components/home/visuals/TwinLifecycleScene.tsx
column3: the teardown count in the shaped lifecycle run. The journal and the reverse replay are real; the resource count is written.

column1: # The careers page is the one place on this site where a percentage is not a
# measurement at all. These are the terms of an offer: the equity ranges for the
# two founding roles, set by the founder, which the page states before it
# describes either role. There is nothing to source them to because they are not
# a claim about how the product performs; they are what is on the table, and the
# page is the source. Deleting them, which is the other answer this file offers,
# would leave a careers page that describes the work and hides the compensation,
# which is the exact thing it was written not to do.
www/components/pages/company/Careers.tsx
